articles.summary:
Researchers have uncovered a campaign in which hijacked GitHub accounts spread secret-stealing malware across thousands of repositories. The payload executed in at least 1,806 repos, exfiltrating CI/CD secrets and cloud credentials.

articles.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

articles.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. A coding agent opens hundreds of files, launches command-line tools and connects to an internal service to complete a task. A support agent authenticates to several systems, retrieves customer records and updates another application. A workflow agent enumerates cloud resources in seconds, then moves to the next stage of its assignment.

clusters.title: AI-written patches are becoming attack maps for hackers
clusters.summary:
This summer, the maintainers of vm2, an open-source JavaScript sandboxing library with 1 million downloads per week, shipped fixes for 34 separate sandbox-escape vulnerabilities and Anthropic’s Claude co-wrote 19 of them. Weeks later, a security researcher pointed an AI agent at one of the advisories and asked for a way around the patch. The agent delivered.

clusters.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
clusters.summary:
Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records.

The records, which Amazon's threat intelligence team captured with decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys.

clusters.title: Italy Fines Meta €805 Million Over Facebook's Android Gallery Access Without Explicit Consent
clusters.summary:
Meta was fined €805 million in Italy yesterday over a Facebook for Android feature that suggests photos and videos from users' phone galleries for them to post.

The Garante, Italy's data protection authority, found that the feature was enabled by default and that the app accessed Italian users' photos, videos, and related metadata without their explicit consent.

clusters.summary:
The compromise of Anthropic's official Claude Code extension on Cursor's extension marketplace was the result of the theft of an access key that was exposed in the wake of a breach targeting Fireworks AI.

clusters.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
clusters.summary:

clusters.title: The firewall becomes the foothold: Attackers turn Check Point gateways against customers
clusters.summary:
A firewall is intended to be a boundary attackers can’t cross.
But firewalls face the web, making them just as vulnerable to attack as other systems, as evidenced by the emergency hotfixes released by Check Point Software for several of its products. The patches address a high-severity privilege escalation flaw, CVE-2026-123039, that gives attackers root privilege access and the ability to send commands to the Gaia OS Dynamic CLI daemon, a core background process.

clusters.title: Thousands of GitHub repos hit with secret-stealing malware
clusters.summary:
Researchers have uncovered a campaign in which hijacked GitHub accounts spread secret-stealing malware across thousands of repositories. The payload executed in at least 1,806 repos, exfiltrating CI/CD secrets and cloud credentials.

clusters.title: ArcticRAT Cybercrime Gang Profiles Victim Finances With AI
clusters.summary: The Android malware has expanded from focusing on cryptocurrency theft to full device control, and the attackers have added advanced analysis of stolen information.

clusters.title: How AI is changing the nature of cyberattacks
clusters.summary:
AI may be helping cyberattackers increase the speed and scale of their operations, but it is not yet changing their core objectives or the techniques they employ as part of their attack chains.
Phishing, malware, and vulnerability exploitation remain the main techniques in play even as abuse of AI tools has made attacks easier to mount and cheaper for even relatively unskilled attackers, according to security experts.

clusters.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE
clusters.summary:
A type confusion flaw in PostgreSQL lets a database user who can create objects run code on the server. Updates released yesterday fix it, along with 51 other security flaws. Full protection from this flaw also requires rebuilding any C-language extensions installed on the server.

clusters.title: New Mior and Skyfall Attacks Let Rogue Cloud Hosts Steal Secrets From AMD SEV-SNP VMs
clusters.summary:
Two attacks made public this week allow a malicious host to read data inside AMD SEV-SNP-protected virtual machines (VMs), which are built to keep the server's operator out.

One of them, Mior, can also modify a VM's memory and fake the signed report confirming which software it runs. Both need control of the server's hypervisor, and Mior also needs control of the server's BIOS. Researchers

clusters.title: Attackers in Binance Breach Targeted Known Weakness, Missing Controls
clusters.summary: Blockchain complexities, such as attacker-deployed sweepers, hobble security controls designed to limit the damage of an exchange compromise.

clusters.summary:
On the morning of Sept. 3, ChatGPT, Claude and Grok all went down within a few hours of one another. OpenAI blamed a routing error, Anthropic cited an infrastructure issue and xAI gave no cause. Service was back by early afternoon, and most of the coverage focused on people who couldn’t write, code or research for a morning.

clusters.summary:
Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 is reporting today that it has tracked a massive China-based attack leveraging the open-source AI penetration testing framework Cairn to autonomously conduct 25 operations against at least 19 organizations. The attackers weaponized Cairn by pairing it with Chinese AI models Zhipu GLM and DeepSeek, Unit 42 said.

clusters.summary:
An active threat campaign is combining port scanning, password guessing, and Transact-SQL (T-SQL) commands to compromise exposed Microsoft SQL servers and deliver malware.
The attackers are using predefined username and password lists to brute-force into these servers and exploit their administrative capabilities to execute commands on the underlying Windows systems.

clusters.title: AI found Linux kernel bugs that remained undetected for decades
clusters.summary:
A Microsoft research project combining AI agents with human security researchers uncovered 59 Linux kernel vulnerabilities, including bugs that had survived in production code for more than 20 years.
While AI dramatically accelerated the discovery process, the researchers found that validating flaws, developing patches, and working with maintainers remained overwhelmingly human-intensive.

clusters.summary: CVE-2026-102895 is a trivial authentication-bypass vulnerability. GPUStack is also an attractive target. It is open-source software that manages clusters of GPUs, which are typically used to run AI workloads. All versions of GPUStack prior to 2.2.0, which was released at the end of June. This vulnerability was not made public until the end of July, and the CVE was assigned on November 4th.

clusters.title: Inside an AI Attack Against a US Retailer
clusters.summary: When hand-typed commands failed to breach a US retailer, the attacker turned to AI-generated scripts, achieving lateral movement in minutes.

clusters.title: The developer laptop just became production. Now what?
clusters.summary:
For decades, enterprise software development relied on an assumption that developers could experiment relatively safely because there were safeguards between their work and production. Development, staging and production had different rules, with human intermediaries making judgments about what was ready to move forward. Testing also assumed that software would behave predictably when executed again.

clusters.title: Hackers stole AI credentials to get $740,000 in free compute; Railway picked up the bill
clusters.summary:
As AI model training and distillation increase, AI tokens are becoming a piping hot currency for threat actors.
Cloud hosting provider Railway found out the hard way; it has confirmed a near 26-hour battle against attackers targeting AI provider credentials to sell to AI ‘transfer stations’ for use in model distillation. The crooks generated about $740,000 in fraudulent AI usage charges using the stolen credentials and potentially had access to up to 100,000 workspace credentials.

clusters.title: Chinese AI Project Scouts Spies in Taiwan Chip Industry
clusters.summary: The CCP built a Big Data system to scrape reams of information and learn about individuals abroad, to potentially target and exploit them. Think Alice Huang Lite.

clusters.title: Japan Pushes Emergency Funding for Cybersecurity as AI-Assisted Breaches Rise
clusters.summary: The package adds public-private cyber responders, an AI-focused team run by the economic ministry, and more leeway to use the government's new active cyber-defense powers.

clusters.title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday November 2026, (Tue, Nov 10th)
clusters.summary: Microsoft continues its AI-induced patch surge, addressing 1,260 different vulnerabilities this month. 68 of these vulnerabilities are considered critical. 167 of the vulnerabilities are Chromium issues affecting Microsoft Edge.

clusters.title: Who Runs the Ransomware Group Qilin?
clusters.summary: The cybercrime group Qilin has emerged as the world's most active ransomware affiliate program, claiming at least 365 victim organizations in the past three months alone. But even top Russian hackers make operational security mistakes, and the administrator of Qilin has made a few key missteps over the last decade that all point to a 36-year-old man living in St. Petersburg, Russia.

clusters.title: Microsoft Fixes Nearly 1,100 Security Vulnerabilities
clusters.summary: Microsoft did another four-digit patch drop today, releasing updates to fix almost 1,100 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and supported software. This month's Patch Tuesday addresses 63 critical flaws -- including a zero-day in Microsoft Outlook -- and comes amid important security updates from other software makers, including Adobe, Apple, Google and Mozilla.

clusters.title: Want to Rent an Internet Address at the White House?
clusters.summary: Several staffers at the White House are using computers or mobile devices equipped with residential proxy services that render their internet address available for others to rent, security experts warned today. One of the proxy services is a Russian company whose founder's web hosting business was ground zero for cyberattacks against election systems in Arizona and Illinois in 2016.

clusters.title: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
clusters.summary: Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user's Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet's access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices

clusters.title: Widespread PHP Flaw May Cause Many Site Outages Today
clusters.summary: Expect to see quite a few websites serving "404" or "Page Not Found" errors today: Nearly 70 percent of websites need to update their core software to fix a pair of vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to seize full control over affected servers. Experts say there are working exploits for the flaws, and that these critical bugs are already being exploited in the wild.

clusters.title: Feds Suspect Ransom Negotiator Ran ShinyHunters Extortion Site
clusters.summary: U.S. federal investigators pursuing the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently stole highly sensitive data from the FBI have identified executives at two different ransomware negotiation firms who maintained unusually close relations with the extortion group, KrebsOnSecurity has learned. Sources close to the investigation say one of the executives in the United States even helped ShinyHunters operate a website that pressured victims into paying a ransom.

clusters.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
clusters.summary: The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.

clusters.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
clusters.summary: Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today's epic patch batch dwarfs September's record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.

clusters.title: FBI Arrests Executive at Ransomware Negotiation Firm
clusters.summary: Agents with the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) on Thursday arrested the co-founder of a Canadian cybersecurity firm in connection with an investigation into the ShinyHunters hacking group that recently relieved the FBI of sensitive data on thousands of agents, multiple sources tell KrebsOnSecurity.

clusters.title: ShinyHunters Extorted Boeing Spin-off Prior to Arrests
clusters.summary: A teenager from Amman, Jordan suspected of leading the prolific data theft and extortion group ShinyHunters has been detained and is reportedly cooperating with the FBI to identify other members of the hacking gang.
